kerry_method_july_verbatim.delivery_vehicle: In this Reporting Period, Kerry calciner oil is delivered to the Basco injection site in bulk tanker trailers rather than in IBC totes as in prior Periods.
kerry_method_july_verbatim.delivery_form: Delivered mass is therefore established from CAT Scale tickets — the full weight less the post-offload empty (tare) weight of the same tractor and trailer — rather than from per-tote tag weights. There is no per-tote record for a tanker load; the scale tickets are the primary mass evidence.
kerry_method_july_verbatim.filtered_mass: For Kerry, that subtraction uses the measured solids content of Kerry calciner oil itself, not the AECN-derived solids content that Charm applies to its other third-party oil.
kerry_method_july_verbatim.testing_location: Testing is in the Additional Documentation folder.
kerry_method_july_verbatim.constants_block_citation: The Kerry solids value and its source analysis are cited on the constants block of the Kerry tab in the weekly ops notes
kerry_method_july_verbatim.loss_treatment: Kerry takes a filtration deduction only. No sparging loss is applied to Kerry oil (because Kerry is not sparged)
kerry_method_july_verbatim.tank_hold: The oil that is unloaded from the truck is held in a dedicated tank and progressively injected in combination with AECN injections as the high viscosity of the oil precludes independent injection.
kerry_method_july_verbatim.removal_completion: trucked Kerry oil is progressively co-injected with AECN over the course of the month and the associated removal is not considered complete until the tank is empty.
kerry_method_july_verbatim.ph: we do not have an independent pH value that is specific to Kerry. Rather, the pH measured over the course of the month’s AECN injections is net of Kerry oil as well.

vvb_guidance.bearing_on_this_batch: July Kerry section governs: ticket pair is the mass evidence, Kerry-specific filtration only, no sparging, tank hold until empty, pH shared with AECN. No section in any of the three docs addresses holding one Kerry tanker load across weeks while a later load is credited first, or the 14-day ticket-to-injection gap.
